en.b_p: Claude Sonnet 5.5 built a DCF and a comps table for each of 50 companies (35 US, 15 European), three ways. Every reported figure was scored against the filing.
b_cards: In the DCFs, numbers it couldn't find and filled in anyway: derived share counts, estimated capex, non-GAAP revenue. In the comps, twelve-month figures a quarter out of date, from an aggregator.
A pre-registered re-run with 30 searches and high effort still wrote a figure that isn't the filing's. The placeholders went away; the cost per table more than doubled.
The runs found gaps in deskstack's own data and two bugs in the scorer. All fixed, tested, and written up with the results.

Daily yields from 1 month to 30 years.
30+ currencies, on a date or averaged over a period.
Equity risk premium by country; betas and cost of capital by industry.
Source, URL, accession or ID, period and as-of date on each figure, so you can open the filing it came from.

faq: Is it free?
Yes. The data connector runs on Cloudflare's free plan with a daily cap shared by everyone, and the code is MIT-licensed. For heavy use, deploy your own copy in a few minutes: self-hosting guide.
Where do the numbers come from?
From the filings themselves: SEC EDGAR for US companies, ESEF reports on filings.xbrl.org for European ones, plus the U.S. Treasury, the ECB and Damodaran's datasets. Every figure carries its source.
Does the server see my workbook?
No. The review scripts run in your own Claude session. The server only sees the values the associate sends to verify_value, and keeps no user data. Privacy.
What doesn't it do?

No share prices and no consensus estimates: a market cap needs a price you provide. European coverage is partial and annual only. Banks and insurers are flagged, since a standard DCF doesn't fit them.
Does it replace a reviewer?
No. It catches what can be checked: figures against filings, formulas against rules, language against a checklist. Everything is a draft until you sign it off.
Is it made by Anthropic?
No. deskstack is an independent open-source project that works with Claude. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
en.f_credit: Data from SEC EDGAR, XBRL International's filings.xbrl.org, the U.S. Treasury, ECB statistics and Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern). SEC XBRL handling builds on open-finance-mcp by Nathanael Johnson.
en.f_disc: Independent open-source project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Data may be incomplete or delayed. Not investment advice.
en.w_p: Claude with web search alone made these errors building DCFs and comps tables. Each was read by hand against the filing, and each is caught by a deskstack check.

/associate: verify_value says Stale and gives the latest twelve months
A quarter written as the year
Boeing net income: the fourth quarter (8,220) as the full year (2,235)
/associate: mismatch against the filed annual figure
Share count derived or from the wrong period
Boeing, Pfizer, GE diluted shares: net income ÷ EPS, a six-month count, a Q1 count
/associate: mismatch, and a flag when diluted shares are more than 10% from the cover page
Non-GAAP or segment figure for the group
GE "adjusted revenue"; Stellantis D&A for industrial activities only
/associate: mismatch against the group's filed line
Figure from an aggregator or Wikipedia
Cisco and Verizon operating income; Schneider operating income, rounded
/associate: mismatch, with the filed value and its source
Estimate typed as a filed figure
Netflix capex as operating cash flow minus free cash flow

en.k_p: deskstack-check checks any .xlsx model, whether Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, another tool or a person built it. Offline, it runs the 20 model checks. With --verify, it also ties every typed figure to the filing; only those figures are sent.
en.k_soon: Soon on PyPI. Today, from a clone: pipx run --spec ./checker deskstack-check model.xlsx.

  MISMATCH  Inputs!C5  Revenue FY2025  416,116  filed 416,161

FAIL (fails on blocker)
en.k_action_p: The GitHub Action checks every workbook on each push and writes the report in the job summary.
en.k_action:
- uses: joaquimmj/deskstack@main
  with:
    files: "models/**/*.xlsx"
    verify: "true"
    fail-on: blocker

faq: Est-ce gratuit ?

Oui. Le connecteur tourne sur l'offre gratuite de Cloudflare avec un plafond quotidien partagé, et le code est sous licence MIT. Pour un usage intensif, déployez votre propre copie en quelques minutes : guide d'auto-hébergement.
D'où viennent les chiffres ?

Des dépôts eux-mêmes : SEC EDGAR pour les sociétés américaines, les rapports ESEF sur filings.xbrl.org pour les européennes, plus le Trésor américain, la BCE et les données de Damodaran. Chaque chiffre porte sa source.
Le serveur voit-il mon classeur ?

Non. Les scripts de revue tournent dans votre propre session Claude. Le serveur ne voit que les valeurs que l'associate envoie à verify_value, et ne conserve aucune donnée utilisateur. Confidentialité.
Que ne fait-il pas ?

Pas de cours de bourse ni de consensus : une capitalisation demande un cours que vous fournissez. La couverture européenne est partielle et annuelle uniquement. Les banques et assureurs sont signalés, un DCF standard ne leur convient pas.
Remplace-t-il un relecteur ?
Non. Il attrape ce qui se vérifie : les chiffres contre les dépôts, les formules contre des règles, le langage contre une checklist. Tout reste un brouillon jusqu'à votre accord.
Est-ce fait par Anthropic ?
Non. deskstack est un projet open source indépendant qui fonctionne avec Claude. Il n'est ni affilié à Anthropic ni approuvé par elle.
fr.end_t2: Avant que quelqu'un d'autre ne le fasse.
fr.f_credit: Données de SEC EDGAR, filings.xbrl.org (XBRL International), du Trésor américain, de la BCE et d'Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern). Le traitement XBRL de la SEC s'appuie sur open-finance-mcp de Nathanael Johnson.
fr.f_disc: Projet open source indépendant. Ni affilié à Anthropic ni approuvé par elle. Les données peuvent être incomplètes ou en retard. Pas un conseil en investissement.
fr.w_p: Claude, avec la seule recherche web, a fait ces erreurs en construisant des DCF et des tableaux de comparables. Chacune a été relue à la main face au dépôt, et chacune est attrapée par un contrôle deskstack.
